title: Own the pieces: why a covered call beats an equivalent cash-secured put
summary: A Wall Street saying: a basket of options is worth more than an option on a basket, so own the pieces. A $95 cash-secured put on a $100 stock is economically the same as a $95 covered call, but the covered call has two line items (stock and call) you can manage separately. So the speaker sells covered calls and almost never cash-secured puts.

steps.caption: A cash-secured put struck at $95: one line item.
A covered call struck at $95: long 100 shares plus one short call. Two line items.
The difference is near zero: by put-call parity the two trades have almost the same payoff.
Both break even at the same price, the strike minus the extra value received.
Same economics, but with the covered call you own the pieces and can manage the stock and the call separately.

takeaways: A basket of options is worth more than an option on a basket, so you would rather own the pieces.
Owning 11 S&P 500 sectors lets you rebalance and capture dispersion, which one index fund does not.
A $95 cash-secured put on a $100 stock equals a $95 covered call economically.
The covered call gives two line items you can manage separately, so the speaker prefers it.
caveats: Small differences remain from rates, dividends and early exercise.
The speaker promotes a waitlist and tools on his website. They are promotional and not verified here.
